newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - BHF bets on success as independent bank.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - BHF bets on success as independent bank.

text.p: BHF-Bank AG, Germany's seventh largest listed bank, on Thursday said it was optimistic for its future as an independent bank after its operating profit rose nearly seven percent in the first nine months of 1996.

Chief executive Wolfgang Strutz told reporters that BHF's operating profit rose 6.6 percent to 258 million marks ($171 million) in the period and said the bank was working hard to restructure internally to maximise earnings.

Key areas for the bank, which is keen to specialise in investment banking, were securities and forex trading, private banking, asset management and the corporate finance business it runs in co-operation with CCF of France and British merchant bank Charterhouse.

BHF's group net interest income rose 4.6 percent to 568 million marks, while net commission income was up by 4.7 percent to 333 million marks. Own-account trading profit was flat at 67 million marks, the bank said.
The figures mark a considerable improvement in earnings growth from the half-year, when BHF could only report a 3.5 percent gain in operating profit for the first six months.

At a time of intense speculation about mergers in the overcrowded German banking market, Strutz said BHF had considered alternatives to independence, "even the unthinkable", but was confident of surviving even without a strong partner.
He noted that Allianz AG Holding, the giant insurance group that owns 15 percent of BHF had said the stake had no strategic intention but that it would not sell it onward to BHF's disadvantage.
The fact that BHF did not sell Allianz products proved that they did not have a strategic alliance, Strutz said.
